stories.title: Saudi-Houthi strikes hit energy and port infrastructure
stories.what: Riyadh, the Houthi-controlled port of Hodeidah and the Saudi terminal at Ras Tanura were hit in an exchange of fire, after a Houthi attack damaged an office tower in Riyadh and Saudi forces struck Hodeidah overnight Tuesday.
stories.why_it_matters: Strikes on a major crude loading terminal and a Red Sea port threaten liftings, raise war-risk premiums and can reroute crude and product tonnage away from the region.
stories.latest: Reported today; Brent is $93.07, up 1.8%, which may partly reflect the strikes.
sources: Riyadh, Hodeidah and Ras Tanura Hit in Saudi-Houthi Exchange of Fire

stories.title: Attacks and escalation around Hormuz
stories.what: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz continue, following tanker incidents near Oman, a mine strike east of Hormuz and a projectile hit on an outbound tanker. Tracking and identity obfuscation around the strait is also in question.
stories.why_it_matters: Hull strikes and mines raise war-risk premiums for Arabian Gulf liftings, slow transits and shrink the pool of willing owners, reshaping crude, product and gas ton-miles.
sources: Riyadh, Hodeidah and Ras Tanura Hit in Saudi-Houthi Exchange of Fire

stories.title: Drone strikes on Russian-linked shipping beyond the Black Sea
stories.what: The Russian RoRo Sparta II was struck by a suspected drone in the Baltic and drifted into Finnish waters. Ukrainian drone boats attacked Russian warships at the port of Benghazi in Libya.
stories.why_it_matters: Strikes in the Baltic and the Mediterranean extend the war-risk zone for merchant shipping far beyond the Black Sea, with implications for insurance cover, routing and port calls.
stories.latest: Libya's Tripoli-based government says it had no knowledge of the Benghazi drone boat attack, and Ukraine denies interfering in Libyan affairs.
sources: Ukraine Denies Interfering in Libyan Affairs After Benghazi Drone Strike

stories.title: Russian refining damage and diesel export limits
stories.what: Ukrainian drone attacks have cut Russian refineries' combined crude processing by 45% since late October, on top of a Russian ban on most diesel exports extended to end-January.
stories.why_it_matters: Lost Russian refining and export restrictions reshape clean product ton-miles, pulling diesel from longer-haul sources and changing MR and LR employment.
sources: Most Large Fuel Tankers Now Ship ‘Dirty’ Crude, Upending Trading

stories.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
stories.what: Sanctions pressure on the shadow fleet is widening, with EU measures targeting shipowners, managers, insurers and financial networks, adding to earlier US designations. The Russian Navy is reported escorting sanctioned dark-fleet tankers in the Mediterranean.
stories.why_it_matters: Designations force charterers and underwriters to re-verify counterparties and vessel positions, and obfuscated signalling makes that verification harder.
sources: Webinar on-Demand Now: Seatrade Maritime News webinar tackles the rising threat of GPS/GNSS attacks on global shipping

stories.title: IMO net-zero rules for LNG and alternative fuels
stories.what: The IMO's Marine Environment Protection Committee opens MEPC85 on 30 November without final rules on how LNG, bio-LNG and e-LNG carbon values are measured under the Net-Zero Framework.
stories.why_it_matters: The accounting treatment of LNG determines the compliance economics of LNG-fuelled tonnage and newbuilding decisions, including LNG carrier and dual-fuel orders now being placed.
stories.latest: No MEPC news today, but Bonny Gas Transport ordered two more LNG carriers at Hudong-Zhonghua and an LNG dual-fuel PCTC entered service for SUARDIAZ.
sources: Nigeria LNG’s BGT orders more vessels from Hudong-Zhonghua
New LNG dual fuel PCTC begins operations with SUARDIAZ Group
